newsitem.title: CHINA: China pledges further reform of state enterprise.
newsitem.headline: China pledges further reform of state enterprise.

text.p: China will form three state holding companies in the chemical, airline and non-ferrous metal industries in a bid to reform its ailing state enterprises, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.

The move was part of a package of measures aimed at adapting the nation's lumbering state enterprises, crippled by poor management and inadequate technology, as China shifts from state planning to a market-oriented economy, it said.

"Those (state enterprises) that have lost their vitality should be eliminated," it quoted Vice Premier Wu Bangguo as saying at a recent meeting on the economy and trade in the northeastern city of Tianjin.
It did not say which companies would be included in the holding companies or give other details of the reorganisation.
The agency said only that details of the plan had been set and that final approval was pending.
Beijing has also been trying to foster large holding companies within the state sector to help boost industrial competitiveness.
It has tried to promote mergers and allow a limited number of bankruptcies, though usually only for small companies.
Beijing has been slow to reform state enterprises, most of which lose money, fearing widespread unemployment and social unrest.
